faq.q: Can I bring my own vegan food on a Marbella boat rental?
faq.a: Yes, absolutely. You are welcome to bring your own vegan food and drinks on any of our charters. Our skipper can store items in the onboard fridge and help serve them during the trip. Just let us know in advance so we can ensure proper storage.

faq.q: What vegan snacks are best for a boat trip in Marbella?
faq.a: Opt for easy-to-eat, non-perishable snacks like fresh fruit (grapes, apples, bananas), vegetable sticks with hummus, nuts, seeds, rice cakes, and plant-based protein bars. Avoid anything that melts quickly, like chocolate, unless stored in a cooler.

faq.q: Are the included drinks and snacks on your charters vegan?
faq.a: Our standard inclusions—water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, and light snacks—may not all be vegan. The snacks are typically non-vegan (e.g., crisps, olives may be fine, but check). We recommend bringing your own vegan alternatives.

faq.q: Where can I buy vegan food near Puerto Banús before my boat rental?
faq.a: Mercadona and Carrefour in Puerto Banús have dedicated vegan sections with plant-based milks, yoghurts, meats, and snacks. For organic options, visit El Corte Inglés or local health food shops in Marbella town centre.

faq.q: Can the skipper prepare vegan meals on board?
faq.a: Our skippers are not chefs, but they can assist with serving and storing pre-prepared food you bring. If you want a cooked vegan meal, consider booking a catering service that delivers to the boat—ask us for recommendations.

faq.q: What should I avoid bringing on a boat for a vegan trip?
faq.a: Avoid glass containers for safety—use reusable plastic or stainless steel. Skip foods that spoil quickly in heat, like vegan mayonnaise or soft cheeses, unless you have a high-quality cooler. Also, avoid messy items like open sauces.

faq.q: Do your boats have fridges or coolers for vegan food?
faq.a: Yes, all our boats are equipped with fridges and coolers to keep your vegan food and drinks cold. For example, the Astondoa 40 has a galley with fridge space. Let us know your needs, and we’ll ensure storage is available.

faq.q: Can I request a vegan-friendly charter package for my Marbella boat rental?
faq.a: While we don’t offer a specific vegan package, we can customise your charter. Contact us via WhatsApp to discuss adding vegan-friendly extras, or we can recommend local providers for plant-based catering.

data.body_html:
Planning a Marbella boat rental what to bring food vegan 2036 trip? Whether you’re cruising the Costa del Sol on a Marbella boat rental for a few hours or a full day, a plant-based diet is easy to manage with a little preparation. This checklist covers everything you need—from snacks to storage—so you can focus on the sun, sea, and stunning views of Puerto Banús.

Why Plan Your Vegan Food for a Boat Trip?

Boat charters from Puerto Banús typically include drinks and light snacks, but these may not be vegan-friendly. By bringing your own food, you ensure every bite aligns with your diet. Plus, with the Mediterranean heat, choosing the right items—like fresh fruit, nuts, and wraps—keeps things simple and mess-free. Our boats have fridges, so cold storage isn’t an issue.

Vegan Food Checklist for Your Charter

Here’s what to pack for a stress-free day on the water. Adjust quantities based on your trip length—2-hour jaunts need less than an 8-hour exploration.

  • Fresh fruit: Grapes, apples, bananas, oranges (easy to eat, no prep).
  • Vegetable sticks & hummus: Carrot, cucumber, celery—pair with single-serve hummus pots.
  • Nuts & seeds: Almonds, cashews, pumpkin seeds—great for energy.
  • Wraps or sandwiches: Use vegan tortillas with avocado, tomato, and lettuce.
  • Plant-based yoghurts: Coconut or soya yoghurt in small pots.
  • Protein bars: Look for vegan-friendly brands (check labels).
  • Rice cakes or crackers: With nut butter or avocado spread.
  • Water: Bring extra bottles; our included drinks are non-alcoholic but limited.

Where to Buy Vegan Food Near Puerto Banús

Stock up before boarding. Mercadona (Calle Ribera, Puerto Banús) has a ‘Hacendado’ vegan range with plant milks, tofu, and veggie burgers. Carrefour (Avda. del Puerto) offers organic produce and vegan snacks. For premium items, try El Corte Inglés in Marbella (Golden Mile). All are within 10 minutes of the marina.

Boat-Specific Tips for Vegan Dining

Our fleet includes boats like the Astondoa 40 (12.5m, 9 pax) and Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax), both with galley fridges. For larger groups on the Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax), the cooler space is generous. Avoid glass containers—use reusable plastic or stainless steel. Pack food in sealable bags to prevent spills. If you’re on a 2-hour trip, light snacks suffice; for 8-hour charters, bring a main meal like a vegan pasta salad or quinoa bowl.

Sample Menu for a Full-Day Vegan Charter

For an 8-hour trip (e.g., €2,299 on an Astondoa 40), consider this menu:

  • Morning: Smoothie (pre-made in a thermos), banana, oat bar.
  • Lunch: Chickpea salad wrap with avocado, cherry tomatoes, and spinach.
  • Afternoon: Hummus with veggie sticks, mixed nuts, apple slices.
  • Drinks: Water, plus our included soft drinks or cava (check vegan status).

What About Catering?

If you prefer not to bring your own, ask us about local vegan catering services that deliver to the boat. We can recommend providers who offer plant-based platters, sushi, or tapas. Contact us via WhatsApp for options—pricing varies. Alternatively, many Marbella restaurants near the marina, like those on the Golden Mile, have vegan menus if you dock for lunch.
